issues.title: MS-GFEM convergence falsely permits nonzero-trace initial guesses

failure_location.quote: converges for any initial guess $\fwp^{(0)} \in \Hone$ strictly monotonically:

issues.failure_explanation: The exact solution belongs to V=H_D^1(Ω), while the local and coarse components of G have ranges assembled inside V. Consequently, starting from u^(0) outside V preserves its nonzero Dirichlet trace at every iteration. For a concrete admissible example, take Ω=(0,1)^2, Γ_D=∂Ω, A=I, b=0, zero right-hand side, u^e=0, and u^(0)=x_1. Every iterate retains trace x_1 and therefore has energy bounded away from zero, contradicting contraction by any fixed θ<1. Equivalently, the global approximation estimate cannot be invoked with an H^1 input outside the exact-solution space required by eq:weakFormGlobal.
issues.overall_effect: The convergence theorem is false for the stated class of initial guesses. Its continuous convergence guarantee is valid only for initial errors satisfying the homogeneous Dirichlet condition; the discrete preconditioner applied in the test-space system is not otherwise changed.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the iteration and its contraction statement to the weak-solution space V=H_D^1(Ω): require u^(0)−u^e∈V, equivalently u^(0)∈V in the homogenized formulation, and retain the same update and contraction factor θ.
issues.why_classification: The H^1(Ω) claim is not a transcription error: the old iteration is defined there, but its V-valued corrections cannot alter a nonzero Dirichlet trace. The repair is local and preserves the natural discrete method and convergence rate, but it withdraws the explicit guarantee for the substantial, coherent class H^1(Ω)\V. This is a limited weakening of an otherwise comparable theorem, so it is moderate rather than minor or serious.

issues.title: Fixed-solution estimate promoted to an unsupported uniform contraction
issues.failure_explanation: Under the divergence-free assumption, the old corollary and eigenvalue decay support equation eq:msgfem:iteration:1 for the fixed exact solution. The proof then treats that one-vector estimate as a bound for I-G on every H^1 function and changes the global Ω-norm to an oversampling-domain norm. A solution-specific inequality supplies neither conclusion. For an arbitrary v in the admissible test space, one must instead define F_v=B(v,·), observe that v is the exact weak solution and Gv its MS-GFEM approximation, and reapply the global corollary on Ω.
issues.overall_effect: The fixed MS-GFEM approximation estimate remains supported, but the contraction recurrence and hence the convergence conclusion of the theorem are not established by the old proof.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: For arbitrary v∈V, define F_v(w)=B(v,w), observe that v is the exact weak solution for this right-hand side and that Gv is its MS-GFEM approximation, and apply the existing coercive global estimate on Ω. Since its constants and eigenvalue threshold are independent of the right-hand side, choose the local dimensions uniformly to obtain ‖(I−G)v‖_{a,Ω}≤θ‖v‖_{a,Ω}, then use the stated error recurrence.
issues.why_classification: The old proof makes a genuine invalid inference from one solution to an operator bound, so this is not a typo. Nevertheless, the uniform estimate follows by a short, routine reapplication of an existing source-supported corollary; it needs no new lemma, construction, or proof architecture and preserves the theorem and contraction rate without weakening.

issues.title: Unspecified partition of unity in the numerical procedure

failure_location.quote: If not stated otherwise, we use $\nOvs = 2$ oversampling layers.

issues.failure_explanation: Equation eq:pu defines a non-singleton class of admissible partitions rather than an experimental choice. The functions χ_j enter the generalized eigenproblem through eq:gevp and enter the discrete fine-level correction through the matrix representing multiplication by χ_j in eq:discrete:RAS1. Thus different admissible choices generally produce different eigenvectors, coarse spaces, and preconditioned operators. Without a selected partition, the old experimental construction and its reported outputs are not uniquely specified.
issues.overall_effect: The theoretical parameterized method remains defined, but the concrete coarse spaces and preconditioners used for the numerical tables and figures cannot be reconstructed uniquely from the old experimental description.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State that every reported simulation used the distance-based partition of unity cited from Toselli–Widlund, and identify this same discretized family χ_j as the one used in both the generalized eigenproblems and the RAS multiplication matrices underlying the reported tables and figures.
issues.why_classification: No unique partition is forced by the old source, so the omission is not a typo. Disclosing the concrete partition actually used is a short, local completion of the experimental algorithm that makes the coarse spaces and operators determinate without changing the theoretical method, numerical claims, rates, or guarantees.

new_version_repair_locator.quote: For all simulations, we choose a distance-based partition of unity as defined in \cite[p.\ 84]{ToselliWidlund2005}.

issues.title: Incomplete input contract for the 3D simulation

failure_location.quote: We construct an artificial velocity field that rotates around the four pipes (see \Cref{fig:3d}c) and use homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions everywhere on the boundary.

issues.failure_explanation: Equation eq:pde requires a source f. The old 3D setup specifies the geometry, mesh, diffusion, velocity field, and homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions, but not f. Both f=0 and f=1 satisfy the active general assumptions and produce different right-hand sides, so the old description does not determine the linear system whose residual history and iteration count are reported. The new version selects f≡1.
issues.overall_effect: The coefficient matrix and preconditioner construction may be determined without f, but the right-hand vector, solution, GMRES residual sequence, iteration count, and associated total run are not uniquely reproducible from the old source.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add f≡1 to the 3D problem specification and state that this is the source used to assemble the right-hand sides for all runs reported in Table tab:3d_comparison.
issues.why_classification: The source cannot be inferred uniquely from the old setup, making the simulation genuinely under-specified rather than typographically malformed. A single local input declaration determines the right-hand side and associated residual histories while leaving the geometry, operator, preconditioner, and reported type of comparison unchanged; no new mathematical argument is required.
